nodes.content: Develop a shared-control robot that distinguishes human intent changes from reactions to its assistance during collaborative object transport.
requirements: Achieve intent-change F1 ≥0.85 for unseen partners when robot assistance itself induces human corrections.
Reduce unnecessary control overrides by 30% versus a fixed-assistance baseline without increasing peak interaction forces.

nodes.content: Use counterfactual robot-action force predictions to isolate intent changes from assistance-induced corrections; uncertainty-gate overrides and cap interaction forces.
Can counterfactual force residuals distinguish route changes from assistance-induced corrections for unseen partners when robot impedance shifts?
Impedance-conditioned counterfactual force residuals achieve intent-change F1 ≥0.85 for unseen partners across robot impedance shifts.
Collect labeled intent-change and assistance-reaction trials across safe impedance shifts; train a counterfactual-residual classifier and evaluate leave-one-partner-out F1.
Evaluate intent-change F1 on TransportShift-24 using leave-one-partner-out splits across three impedance settings, comparing conditioned residuals against raw-force features.
On TransportShift-24, impedance-conditioned residuals achieved leave-one-partner-out intent-change F1 0.87 across three settings, versus 0.73 for raw-force features.
Select impedance-conditioned residuals for the intent classifier; test uncertainty-gated overrides separately before deployment.
Run held-out-partner crossover trials with selected residual classifier, comparing force-capped gating against fixed assistance on unnecessary overrides and peak forces.
Crossover report documents 34% fewer unnecessary overrides than fixed assistance and peak interaction forces of 41 N versus 43 N.
Run matched-path assistance-perturbation ablations on TransportShift-24, measuring false intent-change alarms with versus without counterfactual robot-action prediction.
On TransportShift-24 abrupt-impedance matched-path trials, counterfactual prediction increased false intent-change alarms to 27%, versus 12% without prediction.
Mask force transients after abrupt impedance changes; infer intent from sustained handle-heading shifts, confidence-gate overrides, and cap peak forces.
Calibrate a 300-ms impedance-change mask, then test heading-based gating on unseen partners for F1, override reduction, and peak force.
Using the crossover report’s 43 N peak as a safety ceiling, calibrate 300-ms masks and heading thresholds on training partners.
HeadingGate-v1 specifies a 300-ms impedance-switch mask, 12° heading-change threshold sustained for 400 ms, and 43 N force cap.
Does HeadingGate-v1 miss genuine route changes initiated during its 300-ms impedance-switch mask on unseen partners?
HeadingGate-v1 detects ≥85% of route changes initiated during its mask because their heading shifts persist after masking.
On held-out TransportShift-24 partners, trigger route changes during HeadingGate-v1’s 300-ms mask; measure detection recall, latency, and peak forces.
On held-out TransportShift-24 partners, masked-window route changes reached 88% recall, 0.78-s median detection latency, and 42 N peak force.
Stratify held-out TransportShift-24 masked-window route changes by heading-shift duration and switch timing; measure recall against the 85% target.
In additional held-out TransportShift-24 trials spanning heading durations and switch timings, overall masked-window recall was 79%, below 85%.
HeadingGate-v1 reaches ≥85% recall for masked-window route changes with post-mask heading shifts lasting ≥400 ms, despite lower overall recall.
Repeat masked-window route-change trials with new unseen partners, including brief shifts; estimate overall HeadingGate-v1 recall against 85%.
In a new 12-partner TransportShift-24 cohort including brief shifts, HeadingGate-v1 achieved 86% overall masked-window route-change recall.
Stratify unseen-partner TransportShift-24 masked-window trials by post-mask heading persistence; test recall for shifts lasting ≥400 ms against 85%.
In a separate eight-partner TransportShift-24 cohort, ≥400-ms post-mask shifts reached 81% recall, below the hypothesized 85%.
Replay 30 independent unseen-partner masked-window route changes with ≥400-ms post-mask heading persistence; score HeadingGate-v1 recall.
In 30 independent masked-window route-change replays with ≥400-ms post-mask shifts, HeadingGate-v1 detected 27, yielding 90% recall.
Keep HeadingGate-v1 in supervised trials; conflicting 81% and 90% sustained-shift recall requires replication before deployment.
Use force-capped assistance micro-pauses to test whether human corrections persist without assistance; confidence-gate overrides using the observed response.
Can 150-ms assistance micro-pauses distinguish genuine route changes from assistance-induced corrections without increasing peak interaction force?
On unseen partners, 150-ms micro-pauses yield intent-change F1 ≥0.85 while keeping peak interaction force ≤43 N.
Implement randomized 150-ms force-capped micro-pauses; compare persistence-based intent labels against fixed assistance on unseen partners and monitor forces.
Run unseen-partner crossover trials with randomized 150-ms micro-pauses, scoring intent-change F1 and peak force against fixed assistance.
Unseen-partner crossover trials yielded intent-change F1 0.86 with 150-ms micro-pauses; peak force was 42 N versus 43 N fixed-assistance.
Stress-test 150-ms micro-pauses during abrupt impedance switches and simultaneous route changes on unseen partners; measure intent-change F1 and peak force.
During abrupt impedance switches with simultaneous route changes, 150-ms micro-pauses yielded intent-change F1 0.78 and peak force 46 N.
Impedance-aware, force-rate-limited micro-pauses restore unseen-partner intent-change F1 ≥0.85 and peak force ≤43 N during simultaneous switches.
Rate-limit 100-ms assistance ramps; compare intent-change F1 and peak force with unmodified pauses during coincident switches and route changes.
Test 100-ms rate-limited micro-pause ramps on unseen-partner coincident-switch trials; compare intent-change F1 and peak force against unmodified pauses.
On unseen-partner coincident-switch trials, rate-limited pauses achieved intent-change F1 0.86 and 42 N peak force, versus 0.78 and 46 N.
Advance rate-limited micro-pauses to override-reduction testing: nominal pauses passed, but coincident-switch failures required the validated ramp modification.
Run unseen-partner crossover trials comparing rate-limited micro-pauses with fixed assistance for unnecessary overrides, intent-change F1, and peak force.
MicroPause crossover report records intent-change F1 0.86, 33% fewer unnecessary overrides, and 42 N peak force versus 43 N baseline.
Learn partner-adaptive assistance-response kernels from low-amplitude impedance dithers; classify unexplained deviations as intent changes and force-limit confidence-gated overrides.
Calibrate response kernels with ±5% impedance dithers; evaluate unseen-partner intent F1, override reduction, and peak force against fixed assistance.
Collect ±5% impedance-dither trials from 16 TransportShift-24 partners; fit 200-ms force-response kernels under a 43 N limit.
DitherKernel-v1 contains 16 partner-specific 200-ms force-response kernels fitted from ±5% impedance dithers, with a 43 N force limit.
Can DitherKernel-v1 calibrate an unseen partner before their first route change without mistaking dither-induced corrections for intent?
Three seconds of pre-change dithers calibrate DitherKernel-v1 for unseen partners, yielding intent-change F1 ≥0.85 and dither-correction false alarms ≤10%.
On held-out TransportShift-24 partners, adapt DitherKernel-v1 using three seconds of pre-change dithers; score intent-change F1 and dither-correction false-alarm rate.
After three-second calibration, DitherKernel-v1 achieved unseen-partner intent-change F1 0.86 and 8% false alarms on dither-induced corrections.
Repeat three-second DitherKernel-v1 calibration with new partners changing routes during dithers; measure first-change F1 and dither-correction false alarms.
For first route changes during continued dithers after three-second calibration, DitherKernel-v1 scored F1 0.76 and 17% dither-correction false alarms.
After three-second calibration, pausing dithers on heading shifts and freezing kernel updates yields first-change F1 ≥0.85, false alarms ≤10%.
Implement heading-triggered dither pauses and frozen kernel updates; test first-change F1 and dither-correction false alarms after three-second calibration.
On unseen-partner first-change trials, trigger dither pauses at 12° heading shifts; freeze kernel updates and score F1 and false alarms.
With heading-triggered dither pauses, unseen-partner first-change F1 reached 0.86 and dither-correction false alarms fell to 9%.
Stress-test heading-triggered dither pauses under simultaneous impedance switches and first route changes; measure unseen-partner F1 and correction false alarms.
During coincident impedance switches and first route changes, paused dithers yielded unseen-partner F1 0.79 and 14% correction false alarms.
Use paused dithers only without coincident switches; route coincident cases to validated rate-limited micro-pauses.
Switch-aware routing uses paused dithers normally and rate-limited micro-pauses during coincident switches; first-change F1 ≥0.85, correction false alarms ≤10%.
Implement switch-aware routing after three-second calibration; evaluate first-change F1, correction false alarms, and peak force in unseen-partner crossovers.
Compare switch-aware routing with always-paused dithers in unseen-partner crossovers; score first-change F1 and correction false alarms by switch condition.
Without coincident switches, paused dithers achieved first-change F1 0.87 and 8% correction false alarms in unseen-partner crossovers.
Test switch-aware routing on unseen-partner coincident-switch trials, measuring first-change F1, correction false alarms, and peak interaction force.
On unseen-partner coincident-switch first changes, switch-aware routing scored F1 0.81 and 13% correction false alarms; peak force was 42 N.
Keep paused dithers for noncoincident changes (F1 0.87); use standalone rate-limited micro-pauses during switches, since hybrid routing scored 0.81.
After three-second calibration, test paused dithers or switch-triggered standalone micro-pauses on unseen partners’ first changes; score F1 and false alarms.
FirstChange report records unseen-partner F1 0.86, 9% dither-correction false alarms, and 42 N peak force across routed conditions.
Fuse anticipatory gaze and torso orientation with handle forces to identify route changes before assistance-induced corrections; confidence-gate force-limited overrides.
Do gaze and torso cues improve unseen-partner intent-change detection when robot assistance provokes corrective handle forces?
Gaze–torso–force fusion achieves unseen-partner intent-change F1 ≥0.85 during assistance-induced corrections and improves F1 by ≥0.05 over force-only detection.
Collect synchronized gaze, torso, and handle-force traces under assistance perturbations; compare fusion against force-only detection on held-out partners.
Run assistance-perturbation fusion ablations on held-out partners against force-only and MicroPause baselines; score intent F1, overrides, peak force.
On held-out assistance-perturbation trials, fusion scored intent-change F1 0.89 versus 0.82 force-only and 0.86 MicroPause.
Test gaze occlusion and torso misalignment during assistance-induced corrections; compare fusion with MicroPause on F1, overrides, and peak force.
Under gaze occlusion and torso misalignment, fusion F1 fell to 0.77 versus 0.84 force-only and 0.85 MicroPause.
Cue-quality gating preserves fusion’s ≥0.85 intent-change F1 under occlusion by reverting to force-limited MicroPause when gaze or torso reliability drops.
Calibrate gaze and torso reliability scores; switch to force-limited MicroPause below threshold, then test occlusion F1 and peak force.
Evaluate quality-gated fusion versus MicroPause on unseen-partner occlusion trials; measure intent-change F1, unnecessary overrides, and peak force.
On unseen-partner occlusion trials, quality-gated fusion achieved intent-change F1 0.86 and 42 N peak force, matching MicroPause F1 0.86.
Compare quality-gated fusion with FirstChange on occluded, post-calibration dither and coincident-switch first changes; score F1, false alarms, peak force.
On occluded first-change trials, quality-gated fusion achieved F1 0.87 versus FirstChange 0.86; false alarms 8%, peak force 42 N.
Adopt quality-gated fusion with MicroPause fallback: intact cues improve F1, while gating restores occlusion performance, including first changes.
Run unseen-partner mixed-visibility crossover trials of adopted quality-gated fusion versus fixed assistance; score intent F1, override reduction, peak force.
MixedVisibility report records unseen-partner intent-change F1 0.88, 35% fewer unnecessary overrides, and 42 N peak force versus 43 N baseline.

Reduce unnecessary control overrides by 30% versus a fixed-assistance baseline without increasing peak interaction forces.
